chapterTitle: Short Hedges vs Long Hedges, Corporate Hedging Arguments, and Basis Risk Mechanics

scenes.title: The Farmer's Autumn Dilemma
scenes.concept: Alex and Marcus discuss why a grain farmer needs a short hedge while a food manufacturer needs a long hedge.

beatOutlines.textOutline: Alex questions why a farmer would sell futures at harvest if spot prices might surge later.
beatOutlines.speaker: Alex

beatOutlines.textOutline: Marcus explains that hedging neutralizes price risk rather than maximizing speculative upside.
beatOutlines.speaker: Marcus

beatOutlines.textOutline: Alex realizes commercial buyers like food processors face the exact mirror risk and need long hedges.
beatOutlines.speaker: Alex

scenes.title: Curriculum Roadmap: Principles, Corporate Agency, and Basis Risk
scenes.concept: Structured pedagogical roadmap covering hedge classification, corporate governance debate, and basis mechanics.

beatOutlines.textOutline: Module 1 establishes Short vs Long commercial hedge selection rules.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Module 2 explores corporate hedging agency theory and gold producer Snapshot 3.1.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Module 3 unlocks basis risk formulas, convergence, and strengthening dynamics.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: Commercial Matchup: Short Hedge vs Long Hedge
scenes.concept: Side-by-side comparison contrasting short sellers protecting inventory vs long buyers securing input costs.

beatOutlines.textOutline: Define the Short Hedge: sells futures to lock in revenue when already owning or producing the asset.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Define the Long Hedge: buys futures to lock in acquisition costs for scheduled commercial procurement.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Summary invariant: Hedging provides commercial certainty by converting variable spot prices to fixed futures.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: The Corporate Hedging Paradox: Shareholders vs Managers
scenes.concept: Deep dive into John Hull's arguments for and against corporate hedging programs.

beatOutlines.textOutline: Arguments against hedging: Well-diversified shareholders can handle unsystematic price volatility on their own.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Arguments for hedging: Stabilizing cash flows protects debt capacity and avoids costly distress or default.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Competitive hazard: When unhedged competitors gain from market swings, hedged firms face strategic pressure.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: Business Snapshot 3.1: Gold Mining & Central Bank Leases
scenes.concept: Visual process diagram showing how banks borrow physical gold from central banks to hedge miner forward contracts.

beatOutlines.textOutline: Step 1: Gold mining company agrees to sell forward production to an investment bank.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Step 2: Bank borrows gold from a central bank at the gold lease rate, selling spot for cash investment.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Step 3: At maturity, physical mined gold repays central bank; shareholders revolt when spot gold rallies.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: Basis Mechanics: Mathematical Definition & Expiration Convergence
scenes.concept: Rigorous formula breakdown of basis b_t = S_t - F_t and convergence to zero at expiration.

beatOutlines.textOutline: Formula introduction: Basis is spot price minus futures price (b_t = S_t - F_t).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Breakdown of variables: S_t spot asset price, F_t futures price, measured in dollars per unit.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Convergence property: As expiration approaches, arbitrage forces F_T to equal S_T, driving basis to zero.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: The Net Price Theorem: Effective Hedged Price
scenes.concept: Mathematical derivation showing why the effective price realized equals the initial futures price plus final basis.

beatOutlines.textOutline: Net price equation: Realized price equals spot sale plus futures gain: S_2 + (F_1 - F_2).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Algebraic rearrangement proves P_net = F_1 + b_2, proving final price depends solely on basis b_2.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Insight: Hedging transforms volatile spot price risk into substantially smaller basis risk.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: Strengthening vs Weakening Basis Dynamics
scenes.concept: Interactive comparison of basis changes and their asymmetric financial impact on short vs long hedgers.

beatOutlines.textOutline: Strengthening basis occurs when basis increases (b_2 > b_1), boosting short hedger realized revenues.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Weakening basis occurs when basis decreases (b_2 < b_1), lowering net acquisition costs for long hedgers.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Summary table contrasting short and long outcomes under both strengthening and weakening environments.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: Worked Case & Active Recall Quiz: Corn Farmer Short Hedge
scenes.concept: Active recall challenge testing calculation of final basis and effective price realized.

beatOutlines.textOutline: Problem presentation: Farmer shorts at $4.20, sells spot at $3.80, closes futures at $3.82.
beatOutlines.speaker: Alex

beatOutlines.textOutline: Alex analyzes the numbers and identifies that basis dropped to -$0.02.
beatOutlines.speaker: Alex

beatOutlines.textOutline: Marcus confirms: Basis is -$0.02 and effective realized price is $4.18 per bushel.
beatOutlines.speaker: Marcus

scenes.title: Executive Synthesis: The 5 Core Principles of Hedging
scenes.concept: Progressive grouping recap displaying at most 2 rules at a time before final compact overview.

beatOutlines.textOutline: Rule 1 & 2: Short hedge protects sellers from price drops; Long hedge protects buyers from price spikes.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Rule 3: Corporate hedging stabilizes operations and avoids distress, but diversified shareholders may prefer risk.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Rule 4: Gold miners hedged through central bank gold loans, but faced revolt during gold rallies.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Rule 5: Basis equals spot minus futures (b = S - F) and converges to zero at delivery.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Rule 6: Effective price equals initial futures plus final basis (P_net = F_1 + b_2).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Final compact executive overview of all 5 principles.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

summarySteps: Short hedges lock in selling prices; long hedges lock in purchasing costs.
Corporate hedging stabilizes cash flows and prevents financial distress.
Shareholder diversification reduces the need for firms to hedge unsystematic risks.
Gold miners hedged via central bank gold leases, causing shareholder pushback in rallies.
Basis is spot minus futures: b_t = S_t - F_t, converging to zero at maturity.
Effective net price received or paid simplifies to P_net = F_1 + b_2.
Strengthening basis favors short hedgers; weakening basis favors long hedgers.
Hedging transforms volatile spot price risk into smaller, manageable basis risk.
bottomTakeaway: Hedging does not maximize profit—it replaces volatile spot price risk with manageable basis risk.
